title: Rabbi David Tawil: Understanding the Amida- "Mechanics of Ending the Amidah"

chapters.title: Answering Kedushah and Kaddish during Elokai Netzor
chapters.about: Rules for responding to communal prayers while finishing the Amidah

chapters.title: Shortening the Amidah to join the kahal
chapters.about: Options for finishing the Amidah quickly to participate in the repetition

chapters.title: Answering Birkat Kohanim
chapters.about: Permissible responses during the final section of the Amidah

chapters.title: Optional Yirat Ratzon prayer
chapters.about: Customary prayers added after Oseh Shalom

chapters.title: Adding personal requests to the Amidah
chapters.about: Guidelines for inserting personal prayers and Parnasah requests

summary: Rabbi Tawil discusses the halakhic mechanics of concluding the Amidah, specifically focusing on the rules for answering Kedushah and Kaddish while finishing the final prayers. He also addresses the custom of adding personal supplications, the proper way to perform the three steps back, and the importance of pausing before moving after the Amidah.
questions: Can I answer Kedushah or Kaddish if I am still finishing my silent Amidah?
What should I do if I am behind the chazzan during the repetition?
Is it appropriate to add personal prayers like Parnasah requests to the Amidah?
How many steps should I take back at the end of the Amidah?
Why is it important to pause after taking steps back before moving again?
